statements.text: The rational number in the form $\frac{a}{b}$ where $a, b \in Z$, $b \neq 0$. Given $p: R \to R$, $p(x) = x + 3$ and $f: R \to R$, $f(x) = x^2 - 4$.
n, where $n(x) = \frac{x+3}{x^2-4}$, is called an algebraic fractional function or an algebraic fraction.
The domain is R except for the values of x which make the fraction undefined (the set of zeroes of the denominator).
The domain of n(x) is R - {-2, 2}. Formula: $R - \{-2, 2\}$

If p and f are two polynomial functions and z(f) is the set of zeroes of f, then the function n: R - z(f) → R, n(x) = p(x)/f(x) is called a real algebraic fractional function, or briefly an algebraic fraction. Formula: $n: R - z(f) \to R, \ n(x) = \frac{p(x)}{f(x)}$
Note that: the domain of an algebraic fractional function = R - the set of zeroes of the denominator.
The common domain of two or more algebraic fractions is the set of real numbers where the fractions are identified together completely (at the same time).

If $n_1$ and $n_2$ are two algebraic fractions, the domain of $n_1=R-X_1$ (where $X_1$ is the set of zeroes of the denominator of $n_1$) and the domain of $n_2=R-X_2$ (where $X_2$ is the set of zeroes of the denominator of $n_2$), then the common domain of the two fractions is $R-(X_1\cup X_2)$ = R - the set of zeroes of the two denominators of the two fractions.
The common domain of a number of algebraic fractions = R - the set of zeroes of the denominators of these fractions.
